faq.q: Is it worth switching real estate brokerages as an experienced agent?
faq.a: It's worth it when your current brokerage costs you more than it gives back — in fees, in time spent on your own marketing and admin, or in a lack of support. The honest test is to run the real math (your split and every fee) against what a full-service brokerage includes, and weigh the hours you'd get back. Our guides walk you through that comparison without spin.

faq.q: What happens to my pending deals and listings if I switch brokerages in Florida?
faq.a: Your active listings are technically the brokerage's, so transferring them requires your current broker's cooperation and the seller's agreement — it's standard and usually straightforward when handled professionally. Pending deals are typically allowed to close at your current brokerage or transferred by agreement. We help new agents map this out so nothing falls through the cracks during the move.

faq.q: What does it cost to join Adams, Cameron & Co.?
faq.a: Adams Cameron is a full-service brokerage with competitive splits and no separate charge for the marketing, technology, CRM, and transaction tools — those are included. The right way to compare is total take-home after all fees, not the headline split. We'll show you the real numbers for your production level.

faq.q: I'm a top producer. Why would I leave a high split elsewhere?
faq.a: Because the highest split isn't always the most money — or the best life. If you're paying for your own marketing, chasing your own admin, and have no manager to call, a slightly different split with everything included and seven-day non-competing manager support can net more and cost you fewer hours. Run your numbers and see.
